exams.notes: Required for all personal licenses; oral exam only for applicants with certified reading disability
exams.quote: as a precondition to issuance of a personal license, each applicant must pass a written or oral examination developed and administered by the commissioner to ensure the competence of each applicant for license

interval_years.quote: Master licenses expire March 1 of each odd-numbered year after issuance or renewal. Electrical contractor licenses expire March 1 of each even-numbered year after issuance or renewal. All other personal licenses expire two years from the date of original issuance and every two years thereafter.

required.quote: Licensees must attain 16 hours of continuing education acceptable to the board every renewal period.

hours_per_period.quote: Licensees must attain 16 hours of continuing education acceptable to the board every renewal period.

period_years.quote: All other personal licenses expire two years from the date of original issuance and every two years thereafter.

available.quote: The commissioner may enter into reciprocity agreements for personal licenses with another state if approved by the board. Once approved by the board, the commissioner may issue a personal license without requiring the applicant to pass an examination

requirements.value: Applicant must hold valid comparable license in reciprocating state, acquired through equivalent exam and experience requirements, held continuously for at least one year before Minnesota application; not eligible if previously failed MN exam or had license of same/greater class revoked/suspended; not eligible if failed to renew for 2+ years post-expiration.
requirements.quote: The parties to the agreement must administer a statewide licensing program that includes examination and qualifying experience or training comparable to Minnesota's.

bonding_required.quote: As a condition of licensing, each contractor shall give and maintain bond to the state in the penal sum of $25,000.

insurance_required.quote: Each contractor shall have and maintain in effect general liability insurance, which includes premises and operations insurance and products and completed operations insurance, with limits of at least $100,000 per occurrence

definition_quote.value: Electrical work means the installing, altering, repairing, planning, or laying out of electrical wiring, apparatus, or equipment for electrical light, heat, power, technology circuits or systems, or other purposes.
definition_quote.quote: "Electrical work" means the installing, altering, repairing, planning, or laying out of electrical wiring, apparatus, or equipment for electrical light, heat, power, technology circuits or systems, or other purposes.

value: laying out electrical wiring, apparatus, or equipment for electrical light, heat, power, technology circuits or systems
methods_authorized.quote: the installing, altering, repairing, planning, or laying out of electrical wiring, apparatus, or equipment for electrical light, heat, power, technology circuits or systems, or other purposes

license_tiers.quote: Class A master electrician, Class B master electrician, Class A journeyworker electrician, Class B journeyworker electrician, Class A installer, Class B installer, Power limited technician, Satellite system installer, Maintenance electrician, Lineman

residential_project_definition.value: A residential dwelling is a single dwelling unit contained in a one-family, two-family, or multifamily dwelling including a garage and accessory building that can only be used by the residents of the single dwelling unit.
residential_project_definition.quote: A "residential dwelling" is a single dwelling unit that is contained in a one-family, two-family, or multifamily dwelling as defined in the National Electrical Code pursuant to section 326B.35. A residential dwelling includes a garage and accessory building that can only be used by the residents of the single dwelling unit.

value: Electrical components manufactured within limits of property owned or leased by a manufacturer (production employees)
Installation, alteration, or repair of electrical appliance units
Planning, laying out, and installation of heating, ventilating, air conditioning, or refrigeration units
Work by employees of electrical, communications, or railway utilities on utility-owned installations
Electrical work by homeowner on owner-occupied residential dwelling with separate utility service
Elevator work performed by licensed elevator contractors and employees
Technology circuits or systems installed by employees of licensed electrical/technology contractors under master electrician supervision (with exceptions)
HVAC contractor work as described in section 326B.38
scope_exclusions.quote: Electrical components, apparatus, or appliances being manufactured within the limits of property which is owned or leased by a manufacturer and such manufacturer's production employees are not covered by sections 326B.31 to 326B.399.

apprentice_supervision_ratio.value: Licensed individuals shall supervise no more than two unlicensed individuals (three for technology circuits or systems work)
apprentice_supervision_ratio.quote: Except for technology circuits or systems work, licensed individuals shall supervise no more than two unlicensed individuals. For technology circuits or systems work, licensed individuals shall supervise no more than three unlicensed individuals.

qualifier_required.quote: Each contractor must designate a responsible master electrician, satellite system installer, or power limited technician, who shall be responsible for the performance of all electrical work

value: Class A electrical contractor: responsible licensed individual must be a Class A master electrician
Class B electrical contractor: responsible licensed individual must be a Class B master electrician
Technology system contractor: responsible licensed individual must be a licensed power limited technician or licensed master electrician
Satellite system contractor: responsible licensed individual must be a licensed satellite system installer
qualifier_license_requirement_by_contrac.quote: Class A electrical contractor means a licensed contractor whose responsible licensed individual is a licensed Class A master electrician.

journeyman_electrician_experience_altern.quote: An applicant for a Class A journeyworker electrician license shall have had at least four years of experience, acceptable to the commissioner, in wiring for, installing, and repairing electrical wiring, apparatus, or equipment

master_electrician_journeyman_experience.quote: shall have had at least one year of experience, acceptable to the commissioner, as a licensed journeyworker

electrician_continuing_education_hours.quote: Licensees must attain 16 hours of continuing education acceptable to the board every renewal period.

national_electrical_code_reference.quote: the rules and safety standards stated at the time the work is done in the then most current edition of the National Electrical Code as adopted by the National Fire Protection Association, Inc. and approved by the American National Standards Institute

utility_worker_exemption.quote: Employees of any electrical, communications, or railway utility, cable communications company as defined in section 238.02, or a telephone company as defined under section 237.01 or its employees, or of any independent contractor performing work on behalf of any such utility, cable communications company, or telephone company, shall not be required to hold a license under sections 326B.31 to 326B.399

public_liability_insurance_required.quote: Each contractor shall have and maintain in effect general liability insurance, which includes premises and operations insurance and products and completed operations insurance, with limits of at least $100,000 per occurrence, $300,000 aggregate limit for bodily injury, and property damage insurance with limits of at least $50,000
